bull.b: The Anthropic agreement materially improves revenue visibility through a long-duration, contracted lease with a major AI customer. It supports TeraWulf’s strategic shift toward high-performance computing infrastructure and reduces reliance on volatile Bitcoin-mining revenue.

bull.t: HPC platform expansion and leasing growth
bull.b: Rapid growth in HPC leasing demonstrates emerging commercial traction beyond Bitcoin mining. The Muskie campus and additional Lake Mariner capacity provide a sizable development pipeline, potentially increasing recurring infrastructure revenue as contracted sites enter service.

Substantial liquidity and proceeds from selling the Abernathy interest provide funding for committed construction and strategic expansion. Recycling capital from a joint venture into larger controlled assets can improve portfolio focus while reducing immediate dependence on new equity financing.

bear.t: Deep losses and persistent cash burn
bear.b: Severe losses and sustained negative operating and free cash flow show that the current business is not self-funding. Continued construction and scaling require substantial capital, creating ongoing funding risk if project cash generation or lease commencements are delayed.

bear.t: Strained capitalization and high interest burden
bear.b: Very thin reported equity and substantial debt reduce financial flexibility during an intensive build-out cycle. The high cash interest burden consumes liquidity before new capacity contributes revenue, increasing sensitivity to execution delays and refinancing conditions.

bear.t: Execution risk and below-target HPC margins
bear.b: Limited skilled labor and customer-driven design changes create schedule and cost risks across multiple large projects. Reported margins remain well below the long-term target while pre-revenue and fit-out costs are absorbed, potentially delaying the conversion of backlog into durable profitability.
